title: Checks for function/method calls with a mutable parameter in debug_assert!, debug_assert_eq! and debug_assert_ne! macros.
summary: In release builds debug_assert! macros are optimized out by the compiler. Therefore mutating something in a debug_assert! macro results in different behavior between a release and debug build. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for decimal literals used as bit masks in bitwise operations.
summary: Using decimal literals for bit masks can make the code less readable and obscure the intended bit pattern. Binary, hexadecimal, or octal literals make the bit pattern more explicit and easier to understand at a glance. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Warns if there is a better representation for a numeric literal.
summary: Especially for big powers of 2, a hexadecimal representation is usually more readable than a decimal representation. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for the declaration of named constant which contain interior mutability.
summary: Named constants are copied at every use site which means any change to their value will be lost after the newly created value is dropped. e.g. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for construction on unit struct using default.
summary: This adds code complexity and an unnecessary function call. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: It checks for std::iter::Empty::default() and suggests replacing it with std::iter::empty().
summary: std::iter::empty() is the more idiomatic way. Clippy puts this lint in the style group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for usage of unconstrained numeric literals which may cause default numeric fallback in type inference.
summary: To ensure that every numeric type is chosen explicitly rather than implicitly. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for literal calls to Default::default().
summary: It’s easier for the reader if the name of the type is used, rather than the generic Default. Clippy puts this lint in the pedantic group, at the level allow.

title: Displays a warning when a union is declared with the default representation (without a #[repr(C)] attribute).
summary: Unions in Rust have unspecified layout by default, despite many people thinking that they lay out each field at the start of the union (like C does). That is, there are no guarantees about the offset of the fields for unions with multiple non-ZST fields without an explicitly specified layout. These cases may lead to undefined behavior in unsafe blocks. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for definitions (structs, functions, traits, etc.) in mod.rs files. lib.rs and main.rs are not checked.
summary: mod.rs is well-suited to acting as a table of contents — listing submodules and re-exports while leaving definitions to named files. Naming each file after its primary definition keeps filenames descriptive and unique, makes editor tabs and search results easier to scan, and makes the filesystem tree mirror the module tree, so the file layout is uniquely determined by the module structure. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Checks for #[cfg_attr(rustfmt, rustfmt_skip)] and suggests to replace it with #[rustfmt::skip].
summary: Since tool_attributes (rust-lang/rust#44690) are stable now, they should be used instead of the old cfg_attr(rustfmt) attributes. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for #[cfg_attr(feature = "cargo-clippy", ...)] and for #[cfg(feature = "cargo-clippy")] and suggests to replace it with #[cfg_attr(clippy, ...)] or #[cfg(clippy)].
summary: This feature has been deprecated for years and shouldn’t be used anymore. Clippy puts this lint in the suspicious group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for #[deprecated] annotations with a since field that is not a valid semantic version.
summary: Also allows “TBD” to signal future deprecation. For checking the version of the deprecation, it must be a valid semver. Failing that, the contained information is useless. Clippy puts this lint in the correctness group, at the level deny.

title: Checks for usage of *& and *&mut in expressions.
summary: Immediately dereferencing a reference is no-op and makes the code less clear. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Checks for slicing expressions which are equivalent to dereferencing the value.
summary: Some people may prefer to dereference rather than slice. Clippy puts this lint in the restriction group, at the level allow.

title: Detects manual std::default::Default implementations that are identical to a derived implementation.
summary: It is less concise. Clippy puts this lint in the complexity group, at the level warn.

title: Lints against manual PartialOrd and Ord implementations for types with a derived Ord or PartialOrd implementation.
summary: The implementation of these traits must agree (for example for use with sort) so it’s probably a bad idea to use a default-generated Ord implementation with an explicitly defined PartialOrd. title: Checks for types that derive PartialEq and could implement Eq.
summary: If a type T derives PartialEq and all of its members implement Eq, then T can always implement Eq. Implementing Eq allows T to be used in APIs that require Eq types. It also allows structs containing T to derive Eq themselves. Clippy puts this lint in the nursery group, at the level allow.

title: Lints against manual PartialEq implementations for types with a derived Hash implementation.
summary: The implementation of these traits must agree (for example for use with HashMap) so it’s probably a bad idea to use a default-generated Hash implementation with an explicitly defined PartialEq.
